title: Introduction to Docker Buildx knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Introduction to Docker Buildx”?
options: Pass build secrets with ordinary ARG and rely on cleanup to hide them.
Assume every build result automatically appears in the local image store.
Use the full source tree and all local credentials as the build context.
Use reproducible build inputs, suitable cache ordering, and an explicit target/platform/output.
questions.answer_key: Use reproducible build inputs, suitable cache ordering, and an explicit target/platform/output.
questions.explanation: BuildKit/Buildx support advanced caching and outputs; builders and exporters can differ, and secret mounts prevent accidental persistence through ordinary build args.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering introduction to docker buildx, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to introduction to docker buildx fails, which response is best?
options: Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For introduction to docker buildx, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
